title: U.S. House · Tennessee's 5th District
area: Middle Tennessee, including Nashville-area and surrounding counties, under the congressional map Tennessee redrew in May 2026.

context.text: Tennessee redrew its congressional district boundaries in May 2026 (mid-decade redistricting); the filing deadline for U.S. House seats was reopened until May 15, 2026 after the new map was signed into law.
Incumbent Rep. Andy Ogles (R) lost the August 6, 2026 Republican primary to Charlie Hatcher, 53.3% to 46.7% (36,085 to 31,626 votes), so he is not on the November 3 general-election ballot.
Chaz Molder, mayor of Columbia, Tennessee, won the Democratic primary with 40.9% of the vote in a five-candidate field.
Race ratings as of September 2026: Cook Political Report and Inside Elections rate the race Solid Republican; Decision Desk and Sabato's Crystal Ball rate it Safe Republican.

candidates.name: Chaz Molder
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 6 Democratic primary with 40.9% of the vote

summary.text: Chaz Molder is the mayor of Columbia, Tennessee, elected in 2018 at age 27 as the youngest mayor in the city's 200-plus-year history. He is a University of Tennessee and University of Memphis law school graduate running as the Democratic nominee for the open 5th District seat.

background.text: Graduate of Columbia's public schools, the University of Tennessee, and the University of Memphis School of Law.
Elected mayor of Columbia in 2018; as of 2026 has passed eight balanced budgets with no property tax increases and says he saved taxpayers $10.5 million through fiscal management.
Formed the Columbia Mayor's Youth Council as mayor.

priorities.text: Says he will advocate for a ban on stock trading by members of Congress, calling it a matter of ethics and accountability.
Says he is dedicated to lowering costs for Tennessee families, farmers, and seniors, including healthcare, housing, and grocery costs, and to strengthening labor protections.
Says he is committed to lowering healthcare costs and supporting rural hospitals so they can stay open.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for lowering healthcare costs and supporting rural hospitals to keep them open, and for expanding health insurance coverage.
Campaign platform calls for policies that empower workers and strengthen labor protections, including the right to organize.

record.text: As mayor of Columbia, passed eight consecutive balanced budgets without a property tax increase.

candidates.name: Charlie Hatcher
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated incumbent Rep. Andy Ogles in the August 6 Republican primary, 53.3% to 46.7%

summary.text: Charlie Hatcher is a veterinarian and former Tennessee Commissioner of Agriculture (2019–2025) who defeated incumbent Rep. Andy Ogles in the August 2026 Republican primary. He owned a dairy and a livestock veterinary practice before entering government.

background.text: Holds a bachelor's degree in animal science from Middle Tennessee State University and a doctorate in veterinary medicine from the University of Tennessee at Knoxville.
Owned a dairy and a veterinary practice specializing in livestock; served as Tennessee Commissioner of Agriculture from 2019 to 2025.

priorities.text: Ran on his professional and government background: "He's a livestock veterinarian, started eight successful businesses from scratch including the Hatcher Family Dairy. ... For the past seven years he's served Tennessee as the Ag Commissioner."
priorities.quote: He's a livestock veterinarian, started eight successful businesses from scratch including the Hatcher Family Dairy. He's an author, Christian family man. For the past seven years he's served Tennessee as the Ag Commissioner. ... You want something hard done right? Hire a farmer.

priorities.text: Said he would prioritize making the federal government run more efficiently.

record.text: Served as Tennessee Commissioner of Agriculture from 2019 to 2025, appointed by Gov. Bill Lee.

candidates.name: James Johnson

summary.text: James Johnson is an independent candidate on the November 3 general-election ballot for Tennessee's 5th District. Ballotpedia lists no campaign website, biography, or Candidate Connection survey response for him, and he polled 1% in an August 2026 Impact Research survey.
